review_notes: I reviewed all of OriginalBlock78.lean. It has two data definitions (`keyPolynomialBlock78`, `originalBlock78`), one `decide +kernel` certificate (`originalBlockCheck78`), and one evaluation theorem (`originalBlockEval78`). I also read `Integer.Sparse.eval`, `eval_substitute`, `OriginalKey` and `originalLess`, and I counted the uses of the `originalBlockEval*` theorems. The evaluation theorem is stated over `x : OriginalKey → ℝ`. `Sparse.eval` is defined only for ℝ-valued vectors, and the module doc in Integer.lean says the interpretation is intentionally over real moment vectors. Generalising to an arbitrary commutative ring would mean redefining `Sparse.eval` and the lemmas `eval_collectBalanced` and `eval_substitute`. That is a library-wide change outside this file, and the only consumers are real-valued moment certificates. The statement is also the specific instance of an already-general pair of lemmas. The specific keys and `Fin 2886` index type are fixed by the concrete certificate data, and the checked equality `originalBlockCheck78` is exact data that cannot be weakened. I found no useful, low-cost generalisation of any statement here.
